text:
ashley: Heads-up — I'm about to merge a Terraform change to the gpupool module that replaces the flat `subnet_ids` list with a `subnet_map` object for per-az selection. This is a shape+compatibility change and will break older GitOps reconcilers that assume `module.gpupool.subnet_ids` is a list.

kevin: Can you paste the diff/snippet? Is this purely a type change or will it drive resource diffs (new subnets/resources)?

ashley: Snippet:```hcl
# old usage (list)
variable "subnet_ids" { type = list(string) }
resource "aws_instance" "gpu" { subnet_id = element(var.subnet_ids, count.index) }

# new (map)
variable "subnet_map" { type = map(string) }
resource "aws_instance" "gpu" { subnet_id = var.subnet_map[local.az_map[count.index]] }
```
This is mostly a shape change — we keep the same number of subnets, but module outputs also change from `subnet_ids` -> `subnet_map`, and I also added an optional `kms_key_arn` var to remove an ARN->ID lookup.

jamie: Oof — our GitOps helm charts and the cluster-reconciler expect `module.gpupool.subnet_ids` to be a list (they do a `join` and pass to chart values). CI just surfaced a failed preview because `outputs` now produce an object instead of a list.

deploy-bot: gitops-ci: preview failed for `clusters/prod/gpupool` — plan error: incompatible types: expected list, got map. See <https://gitlab.internal/redwood/infra/merge_requests/789>.

samir: Also FYI — the IAM role code references `var.kms_key_id`. Since you added `kms_key_arn`, any module consumers that passed `kms_key_id` will still work for now, but outputs that used to expose `kms_key_id` are gone. We should provide a compatibility shim and state migration guide.

kevin: Rollout plan proposal:
- Bump module minor (v2.x -> v2.y) and add explicit deprecation notes for `subnet_ids` and `kms_key_id`.
- Add compatibility vars: accept both `subnet_ids` (list) and `subnet_map` (map). If `subnet_map` is unset, build it from `subnet_ids` so consumers stay intact.
- Canary: apply to a single non-prod gpupool (eu-west-1) via a GitOps canary branch and smoke tests.
- Add a CI preflight step that detects output type mismatches between current module and module consumers and blocks merges.

jamie: Please also add a quick Helm value validation in the reconciler job. Right now the chart assumes `subnet_list` is a CSV. If we accidentally pass a map the pods will panic during bootstrap.

ashley: Agree. I'll implement a compatibility layer in the module: if `var.subnet_map == null` and `var.subnet_ids != null` then convert: `local.subnet_map = { for idx, id in var.subnet_ids: local.az_map[idx] => id }`. Similar for `kms_key_id` -> `kms_key_arn` using a small lookup helper. I'll add `validation` blocks to fail fast if both are set. I'll also include a `migration.md` with Terraforms state steps. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/1234

samir: Nice. Also add an automated TF plan type-check to CI so we catch this earlier. Example snippet to fail on type changes:```bash
terraform init -backend=false
terraform plan -out=tmp.plan && terraform show -json tmp.plan | jq -e '.resource_changes[] | select(.change.actions != ["no-op"]) | select(.change.before.type != .change.after.type) | .' >/dev/null
if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then echo "Detected type changes in plan"; exit 1; fi
```

kevin: Can we also have the GitOps reconcile pipeline run `terraform show -json` on the live state and compare the output shapes to the planned outputs before applying? That would avoid mid-apply crashes.

jamie: Agreed. I'll add a lightweight Helm value schema check in the reconciler that errors for non-list `subnet_list`.

ashley: I'll open the PR with the shim, docs, tests, and a canary job in `.gitlab-ci.yml`. Target is EOD today. Tagging @samir and @kevin for review.

samir: :thumbsup: Please add a short cost note in the migration doc — some configs may change cross-az routing if the az mapping gets shuffled; run the canary with traffic off.

ashley: Will do. ETA EOD — I'll post updates in this thread when CI passes and when I create the canary branch.
